newsitem.title: KENYA: Reduced activity drags down Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Reduced activity drags down Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Reduced activity dragged the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index down on Monday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index lost 6.51 points to stand at 3037.95. Turnover dropped to 7,232,000 shillings traded on 187,684 shares from 56,511,000 shillings traded on 1,251,667 shares on Friday.
Bourse officials said the market was very quiet with trading concentrated on the normal board.
"We were virtually sitting down in the market. It was very dull," a senior broker said.
"Investors do not have money, but more than that, they have been very disappointed by the poor performance of the new issues for the year 1996," he added.
Rea Vipingo Plantations traded at 10.05 from 10.10 on Friday, while Kenya Airways traded at 9.50 from 9.45 and National Bank of Kenya at 14.50 from 15.
Foreign investors bought 2,000 shares of Kenya Breweries at an unchanged 50 and 68,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 55 and 56.
"If you look at the three shares of Rea Vipingo Plantations, Kenya Airways and National Bank of Kenya, all of which were issued sometime this year, all are trading at a marginal loss," he added.
Rea Vipingo Plantations was offered to the public at 10.50, National Bank of Kenya was offered at 15 while Kenya Airways was offered at 11.25.

Brokers said that with the share certificates of the just concluded Kenya Commercial Bank offer for sale out, speculators would flock to the market seeking to make a profit at the current trading price.

They said the issue attracted a large number of foreign investors who acquired eight percent of the total shareholding. During the issue, the government reduced its shareholding from 70.59 percent to 60 percent.
